title: Replace our getopt_long() with the musl implementation and use it everywhere

notes.body: Is this just to avoid dealing with different behavior in different implementations (various versions of glibc that ship with Linux distributions, the glibc from which our version was taken, various BSD flavors, Solaris, etc.)?

added 3 commits
  • cf785ab0 - Use the musl in-tree getopt_long() everywhere
  • 6de4d7f7 - Merge ws_getopt source files
  • d899ccb5 - ws_getopt: Disable MSVC warning C4244
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/4213/diffs?diff_id=246847703&start_sha=5a833238e79e11417559dc375087c191528b8441)

>Is this just to avoid dealing with different behavior in different implementations (various versions of glibc that ship with Linux distributions, the glibc from which our version was taken, various BSD flavors, Solaris, etc.)?

For the "use everywhere" part yes, and also to save me a lot of grief and some ugly hacks coding for Mingw-w64.

> and also to save me a lot of grief and some ugly hacks coding for Mingw-w64.

I.e., the glibc version we had doesn't work cleanly on MinGW-w64?

I gave-up half-way trying to use it with MinGW-w64, because this change just makes sense even without that, and eliminates all that pain.

The issue was conflicting symbols require some macro black magic, and other difficulties I've since forgotten.
And yes, I think the getopt glibc version won't compile under MinGW because of alloca().

Merge ws_getopt source files

commits_data.title: Use the musl in-tree getopt_long() everywhere
commits_data.message:
Use the musl in-tree getopt_long() everywhere

Besides the obvious limitation of being unavailable on Windows,
the standard is vague about getopt() and getopt_long() has many
non-portable pitfalls and buggy implementations, that increase
the maintainance cost a lot. Also the GNU libc code currently
in the tree is not suited for embedding and is unmaintainable.

Own maintainership for getopt_long() and use the musl implementation
everywhere. This way we don't need to worry if optreset is available,
or if the $OPERATING_SYSTEM version behaves in subtly different ways.

The API is under the Wireshark namespace to avoid conflicts with
system headers.

Side-note, the Mingw-w64 9.0 getopt_long() implementation is buggy
with opterr and known to crash. In my experience it's a headache to
use the embedded getopt implementation if the system provides one.
